To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Akt inhibitor, MK2206, enhances the cytotoxic effect and induces cell death in SKOV3 and in ES2 ovarian cancer cells by different mechanisms.

the Akt inhibitor, MK2206, enhances the cytotoxic effect against ovarian cancer cells by inhibiting the Akt pathway in Akt-active cells and by upregulating p53 levels in Akt-inactive cells, and that the combination therapy of Akt inhibitor, MK 2206, with cytotoxic drugs, paclitaxol (Taxol) and cisplatin, is effective against both Akt-active and -inactive ovarian cancer cells.
the Akt inhibitor, MK2206, enhances the cytotoxic effect and overcomes drug resistance of both Taxol and cisplatin against ovarian cancer cells, through different mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a new strategy to improve the efficacy of chemotherapy in ovarian cancer.
the development of combination therapy involving the Akt inhibitor MK2206 and traditional cytotoxic agents for the treatment of ovarian cancer.
the potential of combination therapy with Akt inhibition to overcome chemotherapy resistance in ovarian cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MK-2206 is an effective agent for combination treatment with paclitaxol and cisplatin, in both Akt-active SKOV3 and Akt-inactive ES2 cells.

MK-2206 is an effective Akt inhibitor that synergizes with cytotoxic agents to enhance cytotoxicity in ovarian cancer cells through multiple mechanisms, which may provide a novel therapeutic strategy for ovarian cancer treatment.
the Akt inhibitor, MK2206, enhances the efficacy of paclitoxel (Taxol®) or cisplatain in ovarian cancer cells by different mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Akt inhibitor, MK2206, enhances the efficacy of Taxol and cisplatin against ovarian cancer cells, either by downregulating Akt and its downstream targets in Akt-active cells or by restoring the expression of p53 in Akt-inactive cells.
Akt inhibition by MK-220 is a promising strategy to enhance the cytotoxicity and overcome chemoresistance of ovarian cancer.
the Akt inhibitor enhances the cytotoxic effects of Taxol or CDDP by different mechanisms in Akt-active SKOV3 and Akt-inactive ES2 cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Akt inhibitor, MK2206, may be a useful adjuvant in combination with Taxol or cisplatine to treat ovarian cancer.

combination therapy of MK-2206 and Taxol or cisplatine is effective in inhibiting the growth of ovarian cancer cells and that this effect is mediated by the inhibition of the Akt/mTOR pathway and/or restoration of p53 levels, as well as the induction of ROS.
the Akt inhibitor, MK2206, may be an ideal candidate to combine with cytotoxic agents to enhance the cytotoxicity against ovarian cancer cells.
